name: Flórián Albert
milestone_by_age_26: Joint top scorer at the 1962 FIFA World Cup at age 21; won Inter-Cities Fairs Cup with Ferencváros in 1965 at 24; named European Footballer of the Year (Ballon d'Or) in 1967 at 26.
early_history_summary: Born in the small town of Hercegszántó near the Yugoslav border, Albert was the son of a blacksmith whose mother died when he was two. He joined Ferencvárosi TC at age 11 after impressing coaches at a talent day, made his senior debut at 17 in November 1958 scoring two goals, and earned his first Hungary cap at 17 in June 1959.
family_context_summary: Son of a blacksmith from Hercegszántó; his mother died when he was two. The family later moved to Budapest where Albert was scouted by Ferencváros at a talent day at age 11. No evidence of financial privilege.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence of family domain expertise in football. His father was a blacksmith and the family was working-class.
evidence_summary: Albert's extraordinary footballing talent was evident from his youth: he joined Ferencváros at 11, debuted for the senior team at 17 scoring twice, and was capped by Hungary within seven months. The Ferencváros youth system and Hungarian national team pipeline provided a structured elite pathway. His working-class background and early loss of his mother created urgency but no financial safety net. By 21 he was joint top scorer at the World Cup, and by 26 he won the Ballon d'Or.

name: Agnetha Fältskog
milestone_by_age_26: Self-penned debut single 'Jag var så kär' topped the Swedish chart in January 1968 at age 17, selling 80,000+ copies; released multiple solo albums through the early 1970s; as a member of ABBA, won the 1974 Eurovision Song Contest with 'Waterloo' at age 24.
early_history_summary: Born in Jönköping, Sweden, Fältskog wrote her first song at age six and began piano lessons at eight. She formed a musical trio as a young teen, then joined the Bernt Enghardt dance band at 15, leaving school to work as a telephonist while performing. Her self-penned breakup song 'Jag var så kär' was discovered by talent scout Little Gerhard and became a #1 hit in Sweden.
family_context_summary: Father was a department store manager with a strong interest in music and show business; mother devoted herself to the household. The family was middle-class and supportive of Agnetha's musical ambitions from an early age.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father showed much interest in music and show business, which likely influenced Agnetha's early musical development, though he was not a professional musician.
evidence_summary: Fältskog's early path was driven by intense self-motivation: writing songs at six, performing in a trio as a young teen, and joining a dance band at 15 while working a day job. Her father's interest in music provided a supportive environment. The Swedish pop music infrastructure (Cupol Records, talent scout Little Gerhard) gave her a distribution channel. Her self-penned debut single topping the charts at 17 demonstrated both songwriting skill and audience reach. The formation of ABBA and Eurovision win in 1974 rode the structural wave of European pop.

name: Robert Downey Jr.
milestone_by_age_26: Cast as a regular on Saturday Night Live for the 1985-86 season at age 20; starred in multiple Brat Pack films including Weird Science (1985), Back to School (1986), Less Than Zero (1987), and The Pick-Up Artist (1987) — by age 26 had appeared in over 15 films.
early_history_summary: Born in Manhattan to underground filmmaker Robert Downey Sr. and actress Elsie Downey, Downey made his screen debut at age five in his father's film Pound (1970). He left Santa Monica High School in his junior year and moved to New York City, working as a busboy while auditioning. His stage debut came at 17 in 'Alms for the Middle Class' at Geva in 1983, followed by rapid film roles from 1984 onward.
family_context_summary: Son of underground filmmaker Robert Downey Sr. and singer-actress Elsie Downey. Grew up immersed in the film world, making his screen debut at five in his father's film. His father was semi-famous for underground comedy films like Putney Swope.
parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents were show business veterans. His father directed avant-garde films and his mother was an actress. This provided direct industry exposure and domain fluency from childhood, though the family was not wealthy — Downey lived in a low-rent apartment after moving to New York.
evidence_summary: Downey Jr.'s early career was catalyzed by being born into a show business family: his father was an underground filmmaker who cast him at age five, providing direct domain exposure. Moving to New York at 17 and auditioning relentlessly built reps, but the family film connection opened doors. The 1980s Brat Pack phenomenon was a structural wave he rode, appearing in multiple films by his early twenties. By 22 he had been in ten films and was profiled by Vanity Fair.

name: Luis Suárez
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Eredivisie title and KNVB Cup with Ajax (2009-10 season) at age 22-23; won the 2011 Copa América with Uruguay at age 24; scored 111 goals in 159 appearances for Ajax before transferring to Liverpool in 2011.
early_history_summary: Born in Salto, Uruguay, Suárez moved to Montevideo at age seven with his parents and six brothers. He played youth football at Urreta before joining Nacional's youth setup at 14. He made his first-team debut for Nacional at 18, scoring 10 goals in 27 matches and winning the Uruguayan title. He transferred to Groningen in 2006 and then Ajax in 2007 for £6.75m.
family_context_summary: Born into a large family with seven brothers; his parents separated when he was young. The family had little money. His childhood sweetheart Sofia Balbi moved to Barcelona, which motivated Suárez to pursue a European career to be closer to her.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence of family domain expertise in football. The family was working-class and Suárez grew up in the Cerro neighbourhood of Montevideo.
evidence_summary: Suárez's path from Uruguayan youth football to European stardom was driven by natural scoring ability and relentless determination. The Nacional youth system and subsequent move to Groningen and then Ajax provided a structured European development pipeline. His poverty and family separation created urgency, while his motivation to join Sofia Balbi in Europe added personal drive. At Ajax he scored 111 goals in 159 appearances and won the Eredivisie, before winning the Copa América with Uruguay at 24.

name: Roger De Vlaeminck
milestone_by_age_26: Won the amateur cyclo-cross world championship in 1968 at age 21; turned professional in 1969 and won his first pro race (Omloop Het Volk); won his first Monument classic, Liège-Bastogne-Liège, in 1970 at age 22; by 26 had won multiple major professional races.
early_history_summary: Born in Eeklo, East Flanders, De Vlaeminck's first love was football, debuting for FC Eeklo at 16. His elder brother Erik's success as a pro cyclist persuaded Roger to try cycling at nearly 17. He raced as a junior in 1965 with one win, then won 25 races in 1966. In 1968, he won the amateur cyclo-cross world championship on the same day his brother Erik won the professional title.
family_context_summary: Born in Eeklo, East Flanders. His elder brother Erik was a successful pro cyclist who won seven cyclo-cross world titles. Roger initially preferred football and played for FC Eeklo before switching to cycling at nearly 17, influenced by his brother's success and earnings.
parent_family_domain_summary: No direct evidence of parental cycling expertise, but his elder brother Erik was a world-class cyclist whose success directly influenced Roger's career choice and provided a sibling-domain apprenticeship.
evidence_summary: De Vlaeminck's cycling career was catalyzed by his elder brother Erik, a world-class cyclo-cross champion who provided a direct sibling-domain apprenticeship. The Belgian cycling ecosystem, particularly the Flandria professional team, offered an elite performance pipeline. Roger's natural physical talent was evident from his rapid progress after starting cycling at 17 — winning 25 races in his second year and the amateur world title at 21. The Flemish cycling culture provided deep domain proximity and frontier geography immersion.

name: Ritchie Blackmore
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Deep Purple in 1968 at age 23; the band's debut album 'Shades of Deep Purple' was released that year and reached #24 on the US Billboard chart; by age 26, Deep Purple had released four studio albums including the landmark 'Deep Purple in Rock' (1970).
early_history_summary: Born in Weston-super-Mare, Blackmore moved to Heston, Middlesex at age two. His father gave him a guitar at 11 on the condition he learn properly, leading to a year of classical guitar lessons. He left school at 15 to work as an apprentice radio mechanic at Heathrow while playing in bands. By the early 1960s he was a session guitarist for Joe Meek's productions and played in The Outlaws and Screaming Lord Sutch's Savages, building deep technical proficiency through years of relentless practice.
family_context_summary: Father bought him his first guitar at 11 and insisted he learn properly, leading to classical guitar lessons. The family moved to Heston, Middlesex, a suburb of west London with proximity to the emerging British rock scene. No evidence of significant financial privilege.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence of parental music industry expertise. His father bought him a guitar and insisted on proper lessons, which provided early structured training, but there is no indication of professional music background in the family.
evidence_summary: Blackmore's path to Deep Purple was built on years of obsessive practice — reportedly five hours daily as a teenager — and deep session experience in London's 1960s music scene. His father's gift of a guitar at 11 and insistence on classical lessons provided foundational technique. Working as a session guitarist for Joe Meek and in bands like The Outlaws and Screaming Lord Sutch's Savages gave him extensive professional reps before co-founding Deep Purple at 23. The British hard rock wave of the late 1960s was a structural tailwind.

name: Vladimir Cosma
milestone_by_age_26: Composed the music for the hit Romanian song 'Să Știi Că Te Mint' at age 15 (c. 1955), which achieved great commercial success in Romania; graduated from the National Conservatory in Bucharest with first prizes in both violin and composition; was touring internationally as a concert violinist by 1964 at age 24.
early_history_summary: Born in Bucharest into a family of musicians — his father Teodor was a renowned pianist and conductor, his mother a composer, his uncle Edgar a composer and conductor, and his grandmother a pianist who studied with Ferruccio Busoni. His father put a violin in his hands at age four. He began composing at 12-13 and composed a hit song at 15. He graduated from the Bucharest Conservatory with two first prizes before moving to Paris in 1963 to study with Nadia Boulanger.
family_context_summary: Born into a deep musical family in Bucharest: father was a renowned pianist and conductor, mother a writer-composer, uncle a composer and conductor, and grandmother a pianist who studied with Busoni. This provided intense early musical immersion from birth.
parent_family_domain_summary: Multiple generations of professional musicians on both sides of the family. His father was a concert pianist and conductor who gave him his first violin at four. His mother was a composer. His uncle conducted the Bucharest Cinematography Orchestra. This is a textbook family-domain apprenticeship in music.
evidence_summary: Cosma's early musical development was profoundly shaped by his family: his father (pianist/conductor), mother (composer), uncle (composer/conductor), and grandmother (pianist, Busoni student) provided a multi-generational musical apprenticeship from birth. Starting violin at four, composing at 12, and writing a hit song at 15 demonstrated exceptional early talent nurtured by this family ecosystem. The Bucharest Conservatory provided elite institutional training, and subsequent study with Nadia Boulanger in Paris extended his network. His world tours as a concert violinist from 1964 built professional reps before his film composing career began at 28.
